insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: ₹3,00,000 / ₹4,00,000 / ₹5,00,000 / ₹10,00,000 (as per tables shown; Individual or Floater variants mentioned)

good.name: Room Rent
good.quote: A. Room (Single Standard A/C room), Boarding and Nursing Expenses
good.explanation: Hospital room coverage is limited to a Single Standard A/C room. This is a standard market feature, but choosing a higher category can trigger extra costs and deductions.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for the first 36 months of continuous coverage. Claims for conditions you already had before buying the policy become payable only after 3 years.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the following listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with us.
good.explanation: Listed specific conditions/surgeries are not covered for the first 24 months. You can claim for these only after completing 2 years of continuous coverage.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illness claims are not covered in the first 30 days, but accidents are covered immediately. This is a standard waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Relevant Pre Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period not exceeding 30 days prior to the date of Hospitalisation
good.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered up to 30 days before admission. This is a basic level of cover and may be tight if investigations/treatment run longer before hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Post Hospitalization expenses incurred up to 60 days after discharge... shall not exceed the sum equivalent to 7% of the hospitalization expenses subject to a maximum of Rs.5,000/- per hospitalization
good.explanation: Post-hospitalization expenses are covered up to 60 days, but capped at 7% of hospitalization expenses and a maximum of ₹5,000 per hospitalization. Follow-up medicines and consultations beyond these limits can become out-of-pocket.

good.name: Modern Treatments
good.quote: Section 4 - Coverage for Modern Treatments... is limited to the amount mentioned in table below; * Sublimit all inclusive with or without hospitalization
good.reference: Coverage – Section 4 and the Modern Treatment table (Page 4-5/10)
good.explanation: Modern treatments are covered but only up to the procedure-wise sub-limits shown in the table. This can materially reduce payouts for expensive new-age procedures even if your Sum Insured is higher.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.quote: There shall be automatic restoration of the Basic Sum Insured by 100% immediately upon exhaustion of the basic sum insured, once during the policy period. It is made clear that such restored Sum Insured can be utilized only for illness /disease/treatment unrelated to the illness /diseases/treatment for which claim/s was/were made.
bad.explanation: Sum Insured is restored by 100% only once in a policy year and only for an unrelated illness. This is restrictive because the restored amount cannot be used for the same disease episode.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Associated medical expenses... do not include Cost of pharmacy and consumables, Cost of implants and medical devices and Cost of diagnostics.
bad.explanation: Pharmacy/consumables, implants/medical devices, and diagnostics are excluded from “Associated medical expenses.” This can lead to significant out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization even when the main bill is covered.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: If Policy Holder chooses a higher room category above the eligibility defined in policy, then proportionate deduction will apply on the Associated Medical Expenses in addition to the difference in room rent.
bad.reference: Definitions – 'Associated medical expenses' (Page 2/10) and Special conditions note (Page 4/10)
bad.explanation: If you take a room above your eligible category, proportionate deduction applies on associated medical expenses (not just the room rent difference). This can sharply reduce claim payouts, so staying within the eligible room category is important.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: The Company will pay... the amount of such expenses as are reasonably and necessarily incurred up-to the limits indicated but not exceeding sum insured in aggregate as stated in the schedule hereto;
bad.explanation: No applied co-pay clause is stated here; it only says claims are payable up to the policy limits and Sum Insured. This generally means you are not required to bear a fixed percentage of every claim (unlike many policies that add 10–20% co-pay), subject to other limits/sub-limits in the wording.

unclear.name: No Claim Bonus
unclear.quote: Where the policy is issued for more than 1 year, the Basic Sum Insured including sublimits, cumulative bonus (if applicable), automatic restoration benefit (if applicable) is for each of the year
unclear.explanation: The wording mentions “cumulative bonus (if applicable)” but does not confirm whether it is available or how much it increases the Sum Insured. You would need the product benefits table/policy schedule to know if any No Claim Bonus applies.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: Cashless facility can be availed only in networked Hospitals
unclear.explanation: Cashless treatment is available only at network hospitals. The document does not state the number or list of network hospitals, which affects how easily you can use cashless claims.
